_: US CPI-U annual averages, 1982-84 = 100, for turning the prices in
Paillard's dated price lists into money a reader today can feel.
Only the years this archive actually holds prices for are here.
1952 to 1979 are the BLS published annual averages, which are given
to one decimal place before 2007. The base year is the latest
complete annual average.
Add the year here BEFORE publishing a price from a new price list.
lib/prices.ts now throws on a year that is missing, because it used
to quietly return the price unadjusted, which reads on the page as a
1976 camera having cost the same in today's money as it did then.
The annual average is the mean of the twelve monthly indexes, and the
BLS table prints it in its own column; both were checked against each
other for every year here.
A caveat worth keeping: the base figure for 2025 was taken from
secondary compilations of the BLS series rather than from a BLS
annual-average table read directly, so it may be revised. Every
adjusted figure on the site is therefore shown rounded and described
as approximate. The 1952-1979 values are the official ones.
CPI measures a general basket of consumer goods. It is the standard
way to do this and it is still a blunt instrument for one camera: it
says nothing about what happened to the Swiss franc, to tariffs, or
to the cost of precision optics in particular. The chart says so.
